Data Science & Software Engineering Intern — Summer 2027 (Full-Time)
Allied Legacy Partners · La Jolla, San Diego, CA (in person) · Full-time, 40 hrs/week · ~10–12 weeks, June–August 2027 
Spend a summer building software, data systems and AI agents that run a real business. You'll own one meaningful project end to end and demo it to leadership at the finish.About the role
We operate and grow community association (HOA) management businesses in California. It's an industry that still runs on PDFs, spreadsheets and phone calls, which means a small team with good software has a real edge.
We've built our own stack to get that edge: a Postgres data platform (Supabase) with hundreds of tables covering every community we manage, internal web apps on Vercel that staff use every day, n8n automations, Slack bots, and AI agents built on the Claude and Gemini APIs. We also work in CINC, HubSpot, RingCentral and Google Workspace. Most of what we build is written with AI coding tools like Claude Code, and we expect you to use them too.
The summer internship is full-time, so it goes deeper than our part-time program. You'll be embedded with the people who built these systems, take on a real project with a real user, and be responsible for getting it working.Your summer project and what you'll work on
Each summer intern owns one primary project, matched to your interests and the business's priorities. Examples of the kind of project we mean:

- An AI agent that turns a new client's records into a working profile. When we take over a community, the prior manager hands us years of ledgers, invoices and statements in no consistent format. Take our extraction pipeline from "works on easy files" to "handles the hard ones," with accuracy measured against hand-checked samples.
- A feature in our vendor bidding (RFP) portal. Contractors submit bids by private link or email; staff compare them and record the board's decision. Build and ship a piece of this with the staff who use it.
- A live leadership dashboard. Replace metrics we currently assemble by hand with a dashboard built on our data platform, including the data checks that make the numbers trustworthy.
- An acquisition and growth intelligence engine. Automate how we source, verify and score California HOA management companies and communities from public data.
Alongside your project, you'll also:

- Build and maintain n8n workflows and Slack bots that connect our systems.
- Clean and validate data in our Postgres platform and HubSpot.
- Help staff with small tooling requests, which is how you'll learn what's actually slow and worth automating.
- Document what you build so it keeps running after you leave.What the summer looks like

- Week 1: onboard. Get access to the tools, read-only to start. Shadow staff, learn the data, and ship a small fix in your first week.
- Weeks 2–3: scope. Pick your project with the founder, talk to the people who will use it, and write a one-page plan: the problem, what "done" means, and how you'll measure it.
- Weeks 4–9: build. Ship working versions early, test them with real users, and iterate. Weekly check-ins keep you unblocked without micromanaging you.
- Final weeks: harden and hand off. Make it reliable, document it, and demo it to leadership: what you built, what you learned, and what should come next.
Everything that touches live data or staff workflows gets reviewed before it goes to production. You'll have room to experiment, with guardrails that keep real communities' records safe.Who we're looking for
We care more about how you think than what you've already learned. You'll fit well if you are:

- A builder who questions the task. You ask whether there's a better way to do something, then test your idea instead of waiting for permission.
- Able to carry a project. You can take a fuzzy goal, break it into steps, and keep it moving across a whole summer with light supervision.
- Hands-on with code. Some experience with Python, SQL, JavaScript/TypeScript, automation tools or AI APIs, through coursework, jobs or personal projects. You're comfortable learning a new tool in a day.
- Careful with details. Our data describes real people's homes and money. Getting it right matters.
- A clear communicator. You can explain what you built and why to someone who isn't technical, and present it to a room.
- Genuinely curious about AI, automation, and how businesses actually run.
You don't need to meet every point to apply. Majors in computer science, data science, engineering, math, economics or anything else are welcome.What you'll get, honestly

- One shipped project with your name on it. A tool or system staff use, plus a demo and write-up you can take into interviews.
- Production experience with applied AI. Building with LLM APIs and AI coding tools against messy real data, not toy datasets.
- A modern stack: Postgres/Supabase, Vercel, n8n, HubSpot, GitHub, and the Claude and Gemini APIs.
- Direct access to the founder and the builders, with weekly check-ins and a final presentation to leadership.
- A reference from people who watched you work, and a path to a part-time role during the school year or a post-graduation offer for strong performers.
What to expect: this is a small team, so structure is light and priorities can shift mid-summer. Some of the work is unglamorous, like cleaning data and verifying records. That's also where you learn how the business really works, and it's often where the best automation ideas come from.
To apply, submit through LinkedIn or Handshake and email your resume and cover letter directly to the founder at david@alliedlegacypartners.com with the subject line:
ALP Summer Tech Intern: {Full Name}, {School}
In your cover letter, briefly cover:

- Why this internship, and how it fits your career goals.
- Relevant experience: coursework, jobs, projects, or things you've built on your own. A link to a GitHub repo, demo or notebook is welcome but not required.
- A time you found a creative or unconventional solution to a problem, or built something that didn't exist yet.
- How you work in unstructured situations with minimal oversight: how you stay motivated and hold yourself accountable.
- Your available start and end dates for summer 2027, and which of the example projects (or one of your own) you'd most want to take on.
Every application is read by the founder. Nothing is screened out automatically.
All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.
